title: Sonam Wangchuk's Wife Vows to Lead Parliament March as Court Upholds Hospital Move
excerpt: Gitanjali Angmo pledges to represent her husband at the July 20 march to Parliament while the Delhi High Court rules his forced hospitalization was lawful.
body:
• Sonam Wangchuk’s wife Gitanjali Angmo says she will lead the march to Parliament on July 20 if her husband cannot participate from his hospital bed.
  • The Delhi High Court ruled Sunday that the government was right to move Wangchuk to Safdarjung Hospital, rejecting his wife’s plea to transfer him to a private facility.
  • Wangchuk, 59, has been fasting since June 28 — now 21 days — in solidarity with the Cockroach Janta Party’s demand that Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resign over exam paper leaks.
  • Angmo alleges a lack of transparency in the hospital’s medical reports and has demanded no treatment be administered without her family’s consent.

The wife of hunger-striking activist Sonam Wangchuk declared on Saturday that she will lead a planned march to India’s Parliament if her husband is too weak to participate, escalating the confrontation between the protest movement and Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government.

Gitanjali Angmo, speaking to reporters outside Safdarjung Hospital in Delhi where Wangchuk was forcibly moved earlier that day, said the campaign would not be stopped by removing its most prominent voice.

“Even if Sonam can’t participate in the march, I will represent him and lead the march on Monday. It’s not that by forcefully removing Sonam they can stop it.”

— Gitanjali Angmo, Wangchuk’s wife

Court Backs Government’s Hospital Move

On Sunday, the Delhi High Court sided with the government, ruling that authorities were justified in moving Wangchuk to the state-run hospital because he had refused to seek medical help despite his deteriorating health.

Judge Mini Pushkarna said doctors had administered only oral fluids and supplements with Wangchuk’s consent, adding that “it cannot be said that any force is being used against Mr Sonam Wangchuk or that his bodily autonomy is being violated in any manner whatsoever.”

Angmo had sought permission to transfer Wangchuk to the privately run Vedanta Hospital, alleging he was being held in “illegal detention.” The court ordered a status report before the next hearing on Friday.

21 Days Without Food

Wangchuk, 59, has been fasting since June 28 in solidarity with India’s Cockroach Janta Party, a youth movement demanding that Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resign over exam paper leaks that affected millions of students in May. The CJP, founded by 30-year-old Abhijeet Dipke, has amassed 22 million Instagram followers since its launch.

Wangchuk had lost more than 9 kg by his 19th day of fasting. His personal physician raised concerns about the risk of hypokalemia — dangerously low potassium levels that can be life-threatening if untreated.

Angmo alleged inconsistencies in hospital reports, claiming Wangchuk’s potassium level had reportedly dropped from 4.3 to 2.9 within 24 hours. She demanded independent testing before any treatment.

March to Parliament

The CJP has called a march to Parliament on Monday, July 20, which coincides with the opening day of the Monsoon Session. The march is expected to draw supporters from across the country, with the movement demanding Pradhan’s resignation and compensation of ₹1 crore for families of students who allegedly died by suicide over exam irregularities.

After Wangchuk was taken from the protest site at Jantar Mantar, CJP founder Dipke began his own hunger strike. Reuters reported that a few hundred supporters returned to the venue later in the day.

A Rare Challenge to Modi’s Government

The campaign has emerged as a rare public challenge to the Modi government, drawing support across political and generational lines. Over 100,000 Instagram reels have been posted urging Wangchuk to end his fast, according to Reuters.

Wangchuk, an engineer and climate activist who inspired Aamir Khan’s character in the 2009 film 3 Idiots, spent six months in jail last year after the government accused him of inciting violence during protests over the federal status of Ladakh. He was released in March and has denied the allegations.

The Safdarjung Hospital said Sunday that Wangchuk’s vital parameters were stable, though his blood parameters remained “marginally altered” and he required sustained monitoring.
image_caption: Climate activist and engineer Sonam Wangchuk has been on a hunger strike since June 28 in solidarity with the Cockroach Janta Party's education reform demands. He was moved to a government hospital on Saturday.
nri_angle: Wangchuk's activism resonates with the Indian diaspora, which has closely followed his campaigns for Ladakh and education reform.
